properties.name: Archimedes diabetes model (2003 described version)
properties.architecture_summary: Continuous-time person-by-person physiological and care-process simulator. Differential equations couple organs, glucose/insulin, complications and treatment effects; equation forms and coefficients are estimated from published clinical/basic/epidemiological data. This meets the ontology parameter-estimated mechanistic inclusion policy. This descriptive paper supplies no own quantitative whole-model validation result; companion validation is cited rather than inherited.
properties.coordinate: Continuous biological and care-process time; no uniform discrete state-cycle approximation

evidence_fragments.content: [paraphrase; visually verified physical PDF page 1] The model is a clinically detailed simulation of diabetes and its complications, people and health-care processes. It is described without mathematical detail in this article; equations and validation are directed to other materials. The abstract reports validation against18trials as an author claim, not primary quantitative validation results shown here.
evidence_fragments.extractor_or_reviewer: Codex parallel source review; no independent human review

evidence_fragments.content: [paraphrase; visually verified physical PDF page 2] Figure1 connects pancreatic insulin production, hepatic glucose, peripheral uptake, blood glucose, HbA1c and complications. The caption distinguishes UKPDS/DCCT data used to build model components from additional trials cited for validation. The arrows define coupled physiological pathways, not a learned neural graph.
evidence_fragments.extractor_or_reviewer: Codex parallel source review; no independent human review

evidence_fragments.content: [paraphrase; visually verified physical PDF page 3] Progression/incidence equations are derived from cohort cumulative-incidence data. Glucose and HbA1c relations use clinical study data including DCCT and UKPDS. Oral-glucose-test values use a modified regression with residual variation. Individual continuous biological variables are translated into noisy measured tests and diagnostic classifications.
evidence_fragments.extractor_or_reviewer: Codex parallel source review; no independent human review

evidence_fragments.content: [paraphrase; visually verified physical PDF page 4] Insulin effects are represented by a factor calibrated using DCCT data, with population variation. Glyburide changes beta-cell insulin production; metformin reduces hepatic glucose production. Doses and combinations change the corresponding biological factors. Diet/exercise affect glucose, lipids, pressure and weight. The reported version omits the metformin weight effect; a later version adds it. Symptoms accumulate perceptually and can trigger care seeking.
evidence_fragments.extractor_or_reviewer: Codex parallel source review; no independent human review

evidence_fragments.content: [paraphrase; visually verified physical PDF page 5] Complications depend on accumulated glycemic exposure over time. Shared individual physiology supplies complication and mortality outcomes. More than100 health-care algorithms specify decisions and follow-up; an example starts lovastatin using LDL and creatinine thresholds, retests after two months, and may change drug. Patient pathways consume visits, time and costs;37office-visit types are represented. Equation forms and coefficients are chosen to fit biological, epidemiological and clinical data.
evidence_fragments.extractor_or_reviewer: Codex parallel source review; no independent human review

evidence_fragments.content: [paraphrase; visually verified physical PDF page 6] The programmed model uses object-oriented Smalltalk and continuous time/variables rather than fixed discrete disease-state cycles. Components are debugged against known quantities and combined; more complex trial simulation is described as the final testing step. Person and organ details interact in a single simulated health-care system. These are implementation/testing descriptions without a table of independent predictive errors in this paper. Intended applications include guidelines, performance measures, disease management, quality improvement, timing of treatment, resource use and cost-effectiveness. These purposes motivate continuous-time biological detail and an integrated reusable model.
evidence_fragments.extractor_or_reviewer: Codex parallel source review; no independent human review

evidence_fragments.content: [paraphrase; visually verified physical PDF page 7] The discussion acknowledges uncertainty and abstraction in biological knowledge and does not claim a perfectly accurate description of diabetes. Trial data can introduce random and systematic error, including limited transport to real settings. Equations and assumptions are directed to an online appendix; separate companion validation methods/results are explicitly referenced.
evidence_fragments.extractor_or_reviewer: Codex parallel source review; no independent human review

These are separate evidence sources; bibliography presence does not import their results.

capability_assessments.rationale: An implemented persistent-state continuous-time simulator with empirically estimated mechanistic parameters meets the declared world-model identity policy. The paper describes treatment-conditioned simulations but reports no own evaluated predictive task or representation-quality evaluation. Therefore no demonstrated L0-L4 is assigned; unknown is not not_world_model. Eighteen-trial validation is an author claim pointing to a separate companion paper, not an inherited result.
